title: Varifocal display latency and mechanical reliability
bottleneck: Varifocal displays must shift focus in sync with the eye's gaze within tens of milliseconds, requiring fast eye tracking plus moving optics or switchable liquid-crystal lens stacks. Mechanical actuators wear out and add bulk; LC stacks offer discrete focal planes with switching artifacts. Any lag between gaze and focus reintroduces the very conflict varifocal aims to fix.
why_it_blocks: Without a fast, reliable, compact varifocal mechanism, the vergence-accommodation conflict has no shippable solution, and VR comfort stays capped. The industry has working demos but no productizable path.
current_state: Half Dome 3 demonstrated a 6-layer LC lens stack with 64 focal planes; startups continue development. Durability, cost, and latency at consumer scale are unresolved. Liquid-crystal lens stacks switch between discrete focal planes, and the stepping itself can be perceptible during fast gaze changes.
